title: Notes for Our Dog Sitter
text:
Dear Jenny,

Thank you for taking care of our {adjective} dog, Waffles.

He eats breakfast at seven and dinner at five. Please give him one scoop of dog food and a few {plural noun} as a treat. He likes his bowl to be {adjective}.

Waffles walks twice a day. He will try to {verb} at every squirrel he sees. Hold the leash {adverb} and keep walking.

His favorite toy is a squeaky {noun}. At night, he sleeps on a soft {noun} next to my bed. If he cannot fall asleep, sing him a song about {plural noun}.

Waffles is a little bit afraid of the vacuum and the {noun}. If he hides under the table, give him a hug and a piece of {food}. Please do not let him lick your {body part}.

Last time we went away, he {past tense verb} for an hour when we got back. On Sunday, he will probably be {verb ending in ing} by the front door.

Thanks again,
The Garcia Family

title: Have You Seen Mr. Whiskers?
text:
LOST CAT

Have you seen our cat, Mr. Whiskers? He went missing on Tuesday from our house on Elm Street.

Mr. Whiskers is orange and white with a {adjective} tail. He wears a blue collar with a bell shaped like a {noun}. He weighs about as much as a {noun}. He loves to nap in sunny spots and eat {plural noun}.

If you see him, please do not chase him. Just call his name {adverb} and shake a bag of {plural noun}. He will {verb} right over to you. He also answers to "{silly word}."

UPDATE: WE FOUND HIM!

Mr. Whiskers was never lost. He was curled up in a basket of {plural noun} in the laundry room the whole time. Dad found him when he heard something {verb ending in ing} under the laundry. Mr. Whiskers looked very {adjective}.

Thank you to all our neighbors who helped look. We are having a party with lemonade and {food} on Saturday. Mr. Whiskers {past tense verb} when he heard the news.

text:

Best Costume: Bubbles the goldfish, who came dressed as a {noun}. Bubbles swam {adverb} for the crowd.

Best Dancer: Daisy the dog, who {past tense verb} on her back legs.

Best Friend: Every single pet. Each one went home with a ribbon and a bag of {plural noun}.

All of the owners {past tense verb} with joy. Next year, we will add a prize for the most {adjective} {animal}.

title: Diary of a Goldfish
text:
Monday: Today I swam around my bowl. Then I swam around it again. It was very {adjective}.

Tuesday: The big human named Leo tapped on my glass and said hello. I said hello back, but it came out as bubbles. He fed me fish flakes and a tiny {noun}. Yum!

Wednesday: Leo put a new castle in my bowl. It has a door, two windows, and a picture of {plural noun} on the side. I will {verb} inside it every afternoon.

Thursday: The cat came to visit. She stared at me {adverb} for a long time. I made a {adjective} face at her, and she {past tense verb} away.

Friday: Leo's grandma said I looked like a little {food}. I think that is a compliment.

Saturday: Leo cleaned my bowl. I spent the whole day {verb ending in ing} and blowing {plural noun}.

Sunday: Leo read me a book about {plural noun}. My favorite part was when the {animal} {past tense verb}. Being a fish is the best job in the world, except maybe being a {noun}.

title: Welcome Home, Puppy
text:
Dear Puppy,

Welcome to our family! My name is Ella, and I am going to be your best friend.

Your bed is in the kitchen, next to the {noun}. Your water bowl is blue, and your food bowl is {color}. You may chew on your toys, but please do not chew on Dad's {plural noun}.

In the back yard, you can run and {verb} all day long. There is a tree, a swing, and a garden full of {plural noun}. Please do not dig up Mom's {adjective} flowers.

Our cat, Pickles, is {adjective} but a little shy. If you want to be friends, say hello to her {adverb}.

At night, I will read you a story about a {adjective} dog who saves the day. I will read it {adverb} so you can fall asleep.

I already picked a name for you. Your name is {silly word}.

Love,
Ella

P.S. When I came home from school today, you {past tense verb} so hard that your whole {body part} wiggled.

title: Biscuit's Checkup Report
text:
Patient: Biscuit
Type of Animal: Dog
Age: Four years old

Today Biscuit came in for his yearly checkup. He walked in wagging his tail and wearing a {adjective} sweater.

We checked his ears, his eyes, and his teeth. His teeth are bright and shiny, like a row of {plural noun}. His heart sounded just like a {noun}. He sat on the scale while {verb ending in ing}. He weighs as much as {number} {plural noun}.

Biscuit is healthy and happy. His owner says he likes to {verb} in the back yard and nap on the {noun}.

Doctor's notes: Biscuit should go for a walk every day. He may have one treat after dinner, plus a small bowl of {plural noun} on special days. Please brush his fur {adverb} once a week.

At the end of the visit, Biscuit {past tense verb} and gave the doctor a big lick on the {body part}. We gave him a sticker that says "I Was {adjective} Today!"

title: My Weekend with Shelly the Turtle
text:
This weekend it was my turn to take home Shelly, our class turtle. Here is my report for Mr. Reed.

On Friday, Shelly rode in the back seat next to a bag of {plural noun}. She looked very {adjective} the whole ride.

On Saturday, I fed Shelly some lettuce and a little piece of {food}. She ate it {adverb}. Then I put her on the grass so she could {verb} in the sunshine. My little brother read her a book about {plural noun}. Shelly fell asleep while {verb ending in ing}.

On Sunday, we had a turtle race. Shelly raced against my brother's toy {noun}. It took her {number} minutes to cross the finish line, but she won! We gave her a {adjective} medal made of {plural noun}.

Fun fact: Turtles can hide inside their shells. Shelly hid in hers when Grandpa started to {verb}.

When I put her back in her tank, she {past tense verb} at me. Next time, she wants to come back and meet our {animal}.

title: Meet Clover, Bunny of the Week
text:
Meet Clover, our Bunny of the Week at the Happy Paws Animal Shelter!

Clover is a soft brown bunny with big floppy ears and a {adjective} nose. She is {number} years old and very friendly.

Things Clover loves: carrots, cuddles, and {plural noun}. She also loves to {verb} in the morning while the other bunnies are still sleeping.

Things Clover does not love: loud noises and {plural noun}. When she is surprised, she hops {adverb} to her favorite hiding spot under a {noun}.

Fun fact: Clover can jump as high as a {noun}. Our helpers {past tense verb} the first time they saw it.

Another fun fact: Clover wiggles her {body part} when she is happy.

Clover needs a family who will give her lots of love and a cozy {noun} to sleep in. If you think Clover would be a {adjective} friend, come visit us this Saturday. She will be {verb ending in ing} by the door, waiting to meet you!

title: How to Teach a Dog to Sit
text:
Teaching a dog to sit is easy if you follow these steps. I taught my dog, Noodle, and now he is the best sitter on our street.

Step one: Find a quiet place with no {plural noun} around. Dogs get distracted very easily.

Step two: Hold a treat above your dog's {body part}. Noodle likes treats that smell like {food}.

Step three: Move the treat back over his head {adverb}. His back legs will fold down all by themselves.

Step four: When he sits, say "Good dog!" in a {adjective} voice and give him the treat. You can also {verb} to show him how proud you are.

Step five: Practice every day for {number} days. Some dogs learn fast, and some dogs need more {plural noun}.

The first time I tried, Noodle {past tense verb} and ran off to chase a {noun}. Now he can sit, shake hands, and {verb}.

Next, I am going to teach him to {verb} while {verb ending in ing}.

title: You Are Invited to Pepper's Party
text:
You are invited to a birthday party for Pepper the hamster! Pepper is turning one, and she wants to celebrate with all her friends.

When: Saturday at two o'clock
Where: The Lopez house, in the living room next to the {noun}

What to bring: A small gift for Pepper. She loves sunflower seeds, tiny {plural noun}, and anything {color}.

What to wear: A {adjective} party hat and your fanciest {plural noun}.

At the party, we will play Pin the Tail on the {animal}. We will also watch Pepper run on her wheel. She runs very {adverb}, so do not blink!

We will eat a big cake shaped like a {noun}. Pepper will get her own tiny cake made of carrots and {plural noun}.

Please do not {verb} near Pepper's cage. She gets {adjective} when there is too much noise.

When we practiced singing "Happy Birthday" yesterday, Pepper {past tense verb} with joy. She cannot wait to see you {verb ending in ing} at her party!

Love,
Pepper and Mia
